- Develop and pitch coalition strategies that connect local government priorities (reliability, affordability, resilience, job creation, tax base) with Base’s products; identify and recruit local partners—community organizations, business groups, labor unions, environmental advocates—to amplify support.

- Build and maintain a rigorous tracking system for relationships, commitments, and follow-ups—managing contact information, conversation histories, and next steps so nothing falls through the cracks as you work across dozens of municipalities.

What You'll Bring

- 2-3 years of experience in local government relations, community organizing, public affairs, or campaign work with a track record of building relationships and winning support for initiatives—experience in energy, infrastructure, or economic development is a plus but not required.

- Existing relationships with mayors, city officials, or local stakeholders, or demonstrated ability to quickly build trust with local leaders and community figures.

- Outstanding written and verbal communication skills—you can explain complex products to non-technical audiences, write clear and persuasive materials for local government, and speak confidently in front of city councils and community gatherings.

- Comfort with ambiguity and strong project-management discipline—ability to manage multiple workstreams simultaneously, stay organized across dozens of relationships without an extensive support system, and prioritize effectively in a fast-moving environment.

- Self-starter instincts and genuine interest in understanding communities—curiosity about local economies, politics, and what matters to people in different regions; comfort traveling frequently to different cities and states.

- Strong interpersonal skills and strategic thinking—ability to read a room, build coalitions, find common ground, and be an effective face for Base in diverse local contexts.

- Comfort with systems and data—you'll build and maintain your own tracking tools to manage relationships, keep notes on conversations, and ensure follow-through.

As we've ramped up in-house manufacturing of our Base-designed and Base-sourced battery product, we have an increasing need for a cross-functional planner across our core operations who can make calls when individual functional plans conflict.

The Master Planner owns the operations side of Base’s plan of record. Our material planners, deployments planners, and production planners bring their plans to you. You dig in with each of them to find the gaps, pressure test the assumptions, resolve any constraints, and make the call on the tradeoff.

You are also the individual contributor for production planning. You build and own the master production schedule for BF1 and the factories that follow it, including factory transition and launch planning as we move product generations and stand up new lines.

Base builds most of its own software, and planning tooling is no exception. You will own requirements and direction for our in-house planning systems, working directly with the software team to build the data model, MRP logic, and interfaces that our planners live in. You will also build a fair amount of tooling yourself, because waiting is worse than shipping.

This scope will grow. As Base scales into more products, more geographies, and more factories, we expect this role to take on broader ownership.

What You’ll Do

- Own the operational plan of record. Consolidate the material plan, install and deployments plan, and manufacturing plan into one coherent plan, at daily grain, and keep them in sync when any one of them changes.

- Run the recurring planning cadence (S&OP) with the material, install, and production planners. Review plan versus actuals, surface constraints and gaps, work the root cause with each planner, and make the call.

- Own production scheduling as an individual contributor. Build and continuously update the master production schedule and build plan by line, component, and day, driven by install demand, inventory targets, and capacity.

- Set factory shift schedules and staffing requirements from the build plan, with clear visibility into the inventory and cost implications of schedule changes.

- Manage inventory targets and netting across finished goods, work in progress, and raw material, balancing working capital against the risk of stockout and install cancellations.

- Automate the reporting. Blockers and opportunities across the system should surface on their own.

- Set requirements and direction for Base’s planning software. Work with the Factory and Supply Chain software team to spec the data model, MRP capability, scenario planning, and planner-facing interfaces.

- Build your own tools. As needed, stand up dashboards, planning models, and analysis where a formal software project is not the right answer.

- Partner closely with Finance & Business Operations to keep operational plans tied to the financial plan, demand planning, and company-level targets.

What You'll Bring

- Ability to influence and align people who do not report to you, across manufacturing, supply chain, deployments, software, and finance.

description:
About Base
Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.

About the Role
Base is looking for a Global Supply Manager to own sheet metal and extrusion sourcing for Base's structural metalwork: aesthetic panels, top cover, straps, and extruded aluminum components like the heat plate on the back of our disconnect enclosure. These parts go into Core Batteries, Disconnects, and associated products, built primarily through Sanmina Plant 4 and a network of direct and bridge suppliers.
You'll take over a real, active scope from day one, not build one from scratch. You'll work closely with Base's Metals category lead as we split Metals into focused sub-categories, sheet metal, extrusions, castings, and conductors, so each one gets the depth of attention it needs.

What You’ll Do

- Own the commercial relationship with sheet metal and extrusion suppliers building Base's structural metalwork, as the primary contract manufacturer and a network of direct and bridge suppliers.

- Take over day-to-day ownership of aesthetic panels, top cover, straps, and the aluminum extrusion heat plate, with no dropped continuity during handoff.

- Build and maintain should-cost models for stamped, formed, and extruded parts, decomposed to material, tooling, cycle time, and finishing, to anchor negotiations and drive cost reduction.

- Negotiate piece price, tooling terms, and master agreements with sheet metal and extrusion suppliers, and manage production escalations as the accountable party.

- Establish dual-source or bridge-supply coverage for the highest-risk parts in the category, and partner with engineering and manufacturing on design trade-offs and line-side production issues.

What You'll Bring

- Background sourcing stamped, formed, or extruded metal components, with fluency in tooling economics, process capabilities, and cost drivers across fabrication methods.

- 2+ years sourcing experience in a similar role.

- Experience owning a commercial relationship with a contract manufacturer or metal fabricator directly, including negotiating piece price and tooling terms as the accountable party.

- Comfort qualifying a bridge or backup supplier quickly when a primary vendor slips, without losing sight of the long-term plan.

- Strong organizational and communication skills, and a willingness to travel domestically and internationally, roughly 25% of the time.

About the Team
Base's structural metalwork covers every stamped, formed, and extruded metal part in our systems, from enclosures and panels to covers, straps, and heat management components. As Base ramps Core Battery and Disconnect production, this category has grown past what one person can own well, so we're splitting Metals into focused sub-categories: sheet metal, extrusions, castings, and conductors.
This is a live, active scope with real production stakes. description:

This is the feedback half of the loop. Reliability test tells us what we think will break. The field tells us what actually breaks — usually in a way the test protocol didn't anticipate. Your job is to see it early, sort out what matters, and get it fixed.
You'll build the team as the fleet scales from thousands of units to hundreds of thousands.

What You'll Do

- Own fleet return rate. Set targets, report the real numbers, and be accountable when a failure mode starts trending.

- Lead and grow the team. Hire and develop field quality, failure analysis, and test engineers and technicians. Set the technical bar.

- Drive root cause to closure. Field signal, RMA triage, teardown, failure recreation, corrective action, verification in the fleet. Personally lead the investigations that matter.

- Make the field calls. Swap, pull, stop ship, firmware mitigation, retrofit campaign. Own the analysis and the execution.

- Fix it in design. Turn field failures into design changes with evidence. Bring the field's data into design reviews and hold the change through implementation.

- Own the data. Dashboards, failure taxonomy, and Paretos that say what is actually breaking and at what rate. The Pareto is only worth anything if the failure coding is honest.

- Partner on supplier performance. Close loop with supplier industrialization on 8D/CAPA, and scorecards.

- Own the FA lab. Build the tooling and methods to recreate field failures and confirm fixes.

- Manage cost of poor quality. Warranty spend, truck rolls, and scrap are engineering metrics.

What You'll Bring

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Materials, Physics, or a related field.

- 4+ years in field quality, failure analysis, or design engineering, including 3+ years leading engineers.

- Experience with field-deployed hardware at scale — you've owned a fleet, caught a failure mode in the data, and driven it to closure.

- Strong hardware fundamentals in electronics, battery systems, thermal systems, or complex electromechanical systems. You can hold your own in a teardown and argue about failure physics.

- Triage instinct: given a pile of broken parts and a noisy dataset, you can say what to fix first and defend it.

- Comfortable with Grafana, SQL/BigQuery, and Python to build systems and help engineers build systems that make intelligent use of data.

- Experience driving supplier corrective actions and holding suppliers to schedule and result.

- Judgment on high-stakes field decisions where acting and waiting both cost real money.

- You can brief an exec on fleet risk in five minutes and debug a PCBA with an engineer for five hours.

Preferred Qualifications:

- Battery Energy Storage Systems, inverters, or other grid-connected power hardware.

- Scaling a field quality function alongside a fast-growing fleet.

- Safety-critical hardware, UL/NFPA compliance, or field safety escalations.

- Build the fleet control plane: inventory, identity, activation, telemetry, and operator tooling for a growing network of GPU nodes in the field

- Own out-of-band provisioning and recovery — Redfish/iDRAC automation, network boot, immutable OS images, and the rescue paths that make ad hoc SSH sessions unnecessary

- Develop the node agent: a secure, durable local substrate that establishes trust with the cloud, reports state, receives work, and survives reboots and bad networks

- Design overlay networking and secure connectivity across consumer internet links, and make it boring

- Connect compute to power: integrate dispatch with our energy planning systems so nodes run when power is available and cheap, and back off when the home or the grid needs it

- 8+ years building systems software close to hardware: platform management, firmware, provisioning, fleet orchestration, or backend services that operate physical machines

- Deep experience with server platforms — BMC/iDRAC, Redfish or IPMI, PXE/virtual-media boot, hardware inventory, and remote recovery

- Strong C, C++, Rust, or Go, and comfort moving between a boot log and a distributed service in the same day

- Experience operating fleets you couldn’t walk up to: servers, network gear, vehicles, telecom, or energy hardware

- Judgment about what to build versus adopt — this project leans on industry standards and existing supply chains, not one-off inventions

title: Environmental Health & Safety Engineer
description:
About Base
Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.

About the Role
Base is seeking a EH&S Engineer to support our field operations teams in Texas. As an EHS Engineer, you will perform hazard assessments, incident investigations, work through employees’ safety concerns and issues, as well as strategize with site leaders to prevent/reduce injuries. In addition, you will ensure environmental compliance with all local, state, and federal regulatory requirements applicable to these departments.

What You’ll Do

- Develop and maintain compliance with all applicable regulations and/or guidelines established by Texas Health and Safety Codes, OSHA, NFPA, NIOSH

- Collaborate with department leadership to complete job hazard assessments and implement health and safety policies and procedures

- Execute industrial hygiene studies to analyze manufacturing byproducts against associated human health thresholds

- Inspect facilities, machinery, and safety equipment in order to identify and correct potential hazards, and implement machine guarding when needed

- Complete and maintain documented safety observations from regular hazard identification audits

- Investigate industrial accidents, injuries, or occupational diseases to determine root causes, corrective actions and preventive measures

- Develop safety solutions to resolve EHS hazards/ concerns within cost and schedule constraints following a safety order of precedence to include elimination, substitution, engineering controls, work practice controls, training, and personal protective equipment (PPE) to ensure that safety of personnel, property, and the environment are within acceptable risk boundaries

- Responsible for hazardous and non-hazardous waste management

What You’ll Bring

- Bachelor’s degree in engineering with an emphasis in occupational health and safety and/or environmental engineering

- 3+ years of experience in the design, development and operational oversight of environmental, health and safety disciplines

- Demonstrated ability to research and apply the best industrial and working practices to provide effective services

- Knowledge of process safety management methods, pressure systems, and chemical delivery systems

- Strong knowledge and experience in interpreting, applying and documenting federal, state and local safety and environmental regulations

- Experience with emergency response communication and incident management in incidents involving hazardous and non-hazardous material releases to air, soil, and water

About the Team
The Environmental Health & Safety team is responsible for building and maintaining a culture where safety is embedded into every aspect of our operations. We partner closely with field, warehouse, manufacturing, and leadership teams to proactively identify risks, implement practical safety solutions, and ensure compliance across a rapidly growing operation.

We want to know the efficiencies and deficiencies of our suppliers just as well, if not better, than our own factories. This role focuses on ensuring that suppliers' manufacturing processes are optimized for the production of high-quality, cost-effective products. You will work closely with suppliers and internal teams to drive product and process improvements, manage supply chain issues, and ensure successful integration of new products into mass production. As a player-coach, you will also lead and develop a team of Supplier Development Engineers - staying hands-on in the technical work while growing the capabilities and careers of your team.

What You'll Do

- Lead and develop a team of Supplier Industrialization Engineers, balancing direct technical contribution with coaching, prioritization, and team growth.

- Ramp supplier lines from early prototyping through full-scale production, ensuring readiness across equipment, staffing, and processes.

- Size-up suppliers to see if they are a cultural fit to work with Base on a long-term basis.

- Work directly with suppliers to assess, design, and optimize manufacturing processes to meet production requirements. Ensure suppliers are capable of scaling production without compromising quality.

- Support the supplier qualification process, including auditing manufacturing facilities, production processes, and quality standards.

- Support design for manufacturability reviews in the product design phase as a representative of "the supplier".

- Map out the manufacturing process of our suppliers to understand capacity bottlenecks to be ahead of future growth needs.

- Evaluate the "should cost" of supplier manufacturing strategies to inform the investment value of Base in our suppliers.

What You'll Bring

- Bachelor's Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Physics, or a related field.

- 7+ years of experience in supplier industrialization, supplier quality, or manufacturing engineering, preferably in the consumer electronics, automotive, or industrial sectors.

- 2+ years of experience managing or leading engineering teams, with a track record of developing technical talent.

- Knowledge in multiple manufacturing processes, including injection molding, CNC machining, PCB/PCBA, stamping, and assembly techniques.

- Experience in manufacturing line design and capital costs, to evaluate supplier investment strategies.

- The ability to manage multiple initiatives simultaneously and meet deadlines - both personally and across your team.

- The ability to effectively work with cross-functional teams and suppliers to drive improvements and resolve issues.

- Willingness to travel frequently - the most effective supplier relationships are built face-to-face.

- Own all fund-level accounting and financial reporting for Base's tax equity funds, including capital account maintenance, HLBV calculations, income and loss allocations, and distribution waterfall accounting.

- Lead the monthly, quarterly, and annual close process for each fund, ensuring accurate financial results and reconciliation between fund-level records and corporate accounting in NetSuite.

- Prepare and maintain audit-ready accounting support, including K-1 schedules, capital account statements, financial statement workpapers, and responses to auditor and investor inquiries.

- Design and implement the fund accounting infrastructure, including the chart of accounts, close procedures, reconciliation frameworks, accounting policies, and internal controls to support scalability and audit compliance.

- 3–6+ years in fund accounting, partnership accounting, or tax equity accounting — at a fund administrator, sponsor or developer, bank, or accounting firm.

title: Organic Social Content Intern
description:
About Base
Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.

About the Role
Our marketing team combines creative, customer-focused strategy with data-driven precision to reach the right customers at the right time. We’re hiring an Organic Social Content Manager to build Base into one of the most distinctive, entertaining, and trusted energy brands on social.
You’ll own the day-to-day operation of Base’s organic channels, from developing the content calendar and creating original content to publishing, engaging with our audience, and learning from performance. You’ll turn Base’s products, customers, employees, and mission into platform-native stories people want to watch, share, and join.
This is a hands-on creative role. You’ll develop recurring social series, respond quickly to relevant cultural moments, and personally bring ideas from concept through production. You should be as comfortable scripting and filming a video as you are writing a caption, organizing a calendar, or interpreting performance data.

What You’ll Do

- Own Base’s organic social strategy, content calendar, and publishing cadence across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, X, and emerging platforms.

- Develop original, recurring content series that make Base, energy, and the grid interesting, useful, and fun to follow.

- Concept, script, capture, edit, write, and publish platform-native content, including short-form video, photos, graphics, carousels, and written posts.

- Find compelling stories across Base’s customers, products, installations, employees, markets, and mission, then turn them into content people want to watch and share.

- Balance planned programming with reactive content, moving quickly on trends, customer conversations, cultural moments, and company news when Base has something meaningful to add.

- Maintain the content calendar and manage the workflows behind it, including briefs, assets, approvals, deadlines, and platform-specific adaptations.

- Collaborate with design, marketing, product, operations, and other teams to support launches, events, market expansions, and major company moments.

- Build relationships with Base’s audience by responding to comments and messages, amplifying customer stories and user-generated content, and identifying advocates who can help grow the community.

- Track organic reach, shares, saves, watch time, engagement, audience growth, and the performance of recurring series. Turn those insights into better ideas and stronger future content.

- Stay close to platform changes, emerging formats, internet culture, and the brands and creators setting the standard for social content.

What You’ll Bring

- Experience creating and managing organic social content for a consumer brand, product-led company, creative agency, media company, or similarly fast-moving organization.

- A portfolio of original social work that demonstrates strong ideas, platform-native execution, and measurable audience or engagement growth.

- Hands-on content creation skills. You can take an idea from concept to published post, including scripting, filming, editing, copywriting, and packaging it for the platform.

- Strong short-form video instincts, including hooks, pacing, framing, captions, sound, and storytelling. You are comfortable using mobile-first editing tools such as CapCut, Premiere, or similar software.

- Excellent writing skills and the ability to make a technical or unfamiliar subject feel clear, human, and interesting.

- Deep familiarity with Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, and X, including an understanding of what audiences expect from each platform.

- Strong creative judgment and a high bar for what is worth publishing. You know how to participate in culture without forcing the brand into conversations where it does not belong.

- Comfort working both behind and in front of the camera when the idea calls for it. You can also help coworkers, customers, and partners feel natural on camera.

- A data-informed mindset. You can interpret content performance, explain what worked, and apply those lessons to the next creative cycle.

- Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage a high-output calendar, multiple collaborators, and fast-moving deadlines.

- A proactive, resourceful attitude and comfort creating structure in a fast-paced, high-ownership environment.

Portfolio
Please include a portfolio or links to three to five examples of social content you helped create. For each example, briefly explain the idea, your specific contribution, and what you learned from its performance.

About the Team
The Marketing team at Base is lean, high-ownership, and results-driven. We operate with clear accountability, tight feedback loops, and a strong bias toward action. title: Senior Software Engineer, Frontend
description:
About Base
Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.

About the Role

We're looking for a senior or staff-level frontend engineer to lead development of the customer experience at Base.
Our apps help members understand their energy usage, manage outages, and track the performance of the battery powering their home. You will set the architecture and technical direction of the interfaces that connect real-world energy systems with a clear, simple digital experience - and you'll be the technical anchor others build on.
You'll join a small, high-impact team responsible for the digital front door of Base. In this role, you will lead development of major product surfaces across web and mobile, set frontend architecture and technical direction across the org, partner closely with product and design to shape the roadmap, and ensure we ship fast, reliable software.
This role requires deep frontend expertise, technical leadership, and the ability to translate complex systems into simple experiences that millions of households can rely on.

What You'll Do

- Lead frontend development of the customer experience across Base web and mobile applications.

- Set frontend architecture and technical strategy across multiple product surfaces, not just your own, and define the patterns, tooling, and standards that let the whole org build faster.

- Own major product surfaces end-to-end, from initial concept through production and iteration, including systems you architect from scratch.

- Work closely with backend engineers to design APIs and data models that support product features. Translate complex energy systems into clear, intuitive user experiences.

- Partner with product and design to shape the roadmap and deliver high-impact features. Establish frontend engineering standards and improve developer experience across the stack, including build tooling, testing, and component architecture.

- Mentor engineers and raise the bar for frontend craft across the team.

- Act as a technical lead on cross-team initiatives, weighing in on frontend architecture decisions beyond your immediate team.

- Use analytics and experimentation to improve the member experience over time.

What You'll Bring

- 7+ years of experience building production frontend or full-stack software, with deep expertise in TypeScript and modern web frameworks such as React or Next.js.

- Strong experience designing frontend architecture for complex web applications, including systems used by other engineers or teams, along with a track record of owning products or platforms from concept through launch and iteration - including at least one system you architected from scratch.

- Comfort working across the stack and collaborating closely with backend engineers on APIs and data models.

- Strong product judgment and the ability to translate complex systems into simple user experiences.

- Experience using product analytics, experimentation, and data to guide decisions. Real technical depth - you've gone deep on hard frontend problems (performance, state management, cross-platform architecture, design systems, etc.).

- Experience mentoring engineers and influencing technical direction beyond your own team. First principles thinking, grit, and a bias toward shipping.

America's power grid is failing - electricity costs have risen even as generation gets cheaper, and blackouts are becoming more common. We're building the software that fixes it. Our team owns the entire stack: firmware that controls batteries in thousands of homes, trading algorithms that buy and sell power in real-time markets, distributed commanding systems that orchestrate a growing fleet as a single grid asset, factory software for our Austin manufacturing line, and the product experience that makes it all invisible to homeowners. If you want to write code that physically moves electrons, ships hardware, and reshapes critical infrastructure, this is the job.

title: Global Supply Manager - Raw Materials
description:
About Base
Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.

About the Role
Base is looking for a Global Supply Manager to build and own our raw and bulk materials category from the ground up. You’ll start with adhesives, thermal interface materials (TIM), potting compounds, chemicals, and paint across our Base Core BOM, and expand into the raw materials that will underpin Base’s broader battery and structural materials strategy: lithium, carbon/graphite, anode and cathode materials, electrical steel, aluminum, cold-rolled steel, and copper.

This is a build-from-scratch mandate, not a handoff. You’ll define how Base sources and manages raw materials before we’re locked into supplier relationships reactively, working closely with Base’s Metals and Cells category leads as raw materials strategy intersects both, and partnering with Manufacturing Engineering as Base’s sourcing needs evolve.

What You’ll Do

- Own commercial sourcing for adhesives, TIM, potting compounds, chemicals, and paint across the Base Core BOM, from supplier selection through piece-price negotiation and production support.

- Build Base’s sourcing strategy for upstream battery raw materials, including lithium, carbon/graphite, anode, and cathode materials, to support Base’s battery supply chain as it scales.

- Build Base’s sourcing strategy for electrical steel and other foundational structural materials, including aluminum, cold-rolled steel, and copper.

- Track commodity market dynamics, including pricing, supply risk, and geographic concentration, for each raw material category to inform make-vs-buy and hedging decisions.

- Partner with Base’s Metals and Cells category owners and Manufacturing Engineering to align raw materials strategy across the broader supply chain.

What You'll Bring

- Direct experience owning a raw or bulk materials category at an OEM or industrial manufacturer (lithium, graphite, steel, aluminum, or a comparable commodity), including supplier negotiation and market strategy.

- Comfort building a sourcing strategy and supplier base from scratch, with no existing playbook or incumbent relationships to inherit.

- Fluency in commodity market dynamics, including pricing mechanisms, hedging, and geographic supply concentration, and how they translate into commercial strategy.

- Strong organizational skills to align raw materials strategy with adjacent categories and sourcing roadmaps that are still taking shape.

About the Team
Base’s supply chain team owns every material and component that goes into building and deploying a home battery system at scale. As Base’s raw materials needs scale with it, the company needs expertise it doesn’t have today.
Right now, raw materials like TIM, potting, and chemicals are managed as a side note within other categories, and lithium, graphite, steel, and aluminum sourcing strategy doesn’t exist yet.
This role gets to build that function from the ground up, at a moment when Base’s raw materials needs are scaling quickly, so the sourcing strategy this person builds will directly shape how Base secures and manages those materials going forward.

title: Senior Electronics Design Engineer
description:
About Base
Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.

About the Role
We are looking for a senior level electronics design engineer to own and drive the electrical architecture of Base's energy storage systems —inverters, batteries, and interconnect devices— from concept through high-volume manufacturing and field deployment. This is a foundational leadership role and you will define how Base builds the most reliable, cost-efficient, high-performance batteries and inverters in the world.

This role is for someone who has spent years deep in power electronics and multi-function distributed ECU system design—someone who has personally taken products from napkin sketches to millions of units in the field—and is now ready to lead a team doing the same. You should have a strong point of view on how to design robust, manufacturable energy systems at scale, and the hands-on credibility to back it up. We want a builder who is equally comfortable debugging a gate driver at the bench and setting the technical direction for the entire electrical platform.

What You'll Do

- Set the electrical architecture and technical direction for Base's full product line, including inverters, battery management systems, and microgrid interconnect devices. Own specifications, topology selection, schematic capture, PCB layout strategy, board bring-up, validation, and reliability testing.

- Build, mentor, and lead a team of electrical engineers. Set high standards for design rigor, validation methodology, and documentation. Create an environment where engineers do the best work of their careers.

- Drive LV embedded systems and power converter design and validation across the product portfolio, including inverter power stages, battery pack architectures, and BMS.

- Collaborate firmware, mechanical, test, reliability, and manufacturing teams to move products from prototype to high-volume production.

- Own production end of line testers.

- Debug and resolve complex system-level electrical issues across power, control, and communication domains. Be the person the team turns to when something doesn't make sense.

- Champion continuous product improvement—drive design iterations informed by field data, manufacturing feedback, and evolving performance targets.

What You'll Bring

- 10+ years of experience in electrical system design, with significant time spent on systems like energy storage, inverters, EV charging, motor drives, or similar high-power applications.

- Demonstrated experience taking complex electrical products from initial architecture through production ramp and field deployment—ideally at scale.

- Strong command of PCB design (Altium preferred) and hands-on bring-up skills: you can solder, probe, wire, and debug with the best of them.

- You can write and run a transient thermal simulation in MATLAB or Python

- Familiarity with embedded systems, microcontrollers and their peripherals, and scripting (Python or similar) for test automation and data analysis.

- Working knowledge of control theory as applied to power conversion—loop compensation, sensor bandwidth, filtering, and stability.

- Experience with automotive or industrial communication protocols (CAN, LIN, Ethernet).

- Proficiency with lab equipment including oscilloscopes, power analyzers, function generators, and programmable power supplies.

- A track record of leading or mentoring engineers, with a desire to build and grow a high-performing team.

Preferred Skills

- BSEE or higher, particularly with a focus on power electronics.

- Experience designing products for UL/CSA/IEC certification and regulatory compliance.

- Familiarity with electric motor design, thermal simulation, or mechanical integration.

- Experience in high-volume manufacturing environments and DFM/DFT optimization.

title: Sr. Manufacturing Systems Engineer
description:
About Base
Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.

About the Role
Base is seeking a Test Engineer to facilitate the deployment, sustaining, and improvement of automated manufacturing test systems developed in-house for the production of battery backup systems. As a member of our team, you will ensure the products developed by the team meet world-class expectations and ensure success of the overall project. You must have a genuine passion for engineering and thrive working in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment.

What You’ll Do

- Lead uptime (HW reliability, software faults, maintenance schedules, etc.), cycle time and FPY improvements on manufacturing test equipment.

- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure the manufacturing test equipment meets and exceeds expectations. Understand shortcomings when expectations are not met.

- Perform preemptive data analysis and voice of the customer (VOC) discussions to understand challenges with manufacturing test equipment post deployment, and advocate for solutions that align with both equipment and production goals.

- Understand engineering first principles of test equipment and have a system level grasp of operations to serve as a key contact for the design team and site operations.

- Build and validate test equipment, then deploy to production lines at contract. manufacturers and internally, while verifying tester documentation to ensure a seamless handoff to production.

- Provide ongoing troubleshooting support for these testers after deployment.

- Support equipment troubleshooting and qualification during development and ramp-up of manufacturing equipment.

What You’ll Bring

- 5+ years of experience in electrical test systems design.

- Exposure to a wide variety of test and automation systems, production machinery, industrial sensors, data acquisition, safety, and I/O devices (i.e., pogo-pins, pressure transducers, temperature controllers, current and power meters, PLCs, etc.)

- Hands-on experience designing and building end-of-line and functional test systems

- Experience with Linux and Windows operating systems.

- Understanding of grid simulators, RLC power manipulation, inverter operations, and power system controls.

- Ability to read and understand software code (e.g., TestStand, LabVIEW, Python, Golang, C, C++).

- Experience with CAN bus communications and ability to interpret traces.

- Basic proficiency in PLC programming and troubleshooting (e.g., Allen-Bradley/Siemens).

- Effective at summarizing/presenting data in a manner that is easily digestible to various technical and non-technical audiences.

- Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field, or equivalent experience.

About this Team

Makers of the machines that power tomorrow. The Manufacturing Engineering team owns the interface between a proof of concept and a scalable, profitable product. Our team focuses on how a product can be built, defining the process technology and equipment solutions along the way. We are the feedback loop with the product design team to ensure designs are manufacturable both at cost and scale. The Manufacturing Engineering team owns every aspect of bringing the physical mechanisms of manufacturing a product into the factory.

title: New Markets Strategy
description:
About Base
Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.

About the Role
We are seeking a strategic operator to catalyze Base’s growth in new markets. This role will develop Base’s perspective on new domestic and international markets from first principles, get the team to a ‘yes’, and support a cross-functional team to stand up businesses in new geographies.
This role will translate a deep expertise in distributed energy storage markets into actionable business cases and drive those opportunities to decision and action. You will not move on to the next idea when the team has aligned to move into a market, but be accountable for making it happen alongside Deployments, Growth, Software, Hardware, and Policy.

What You’ll Do

- Become Base’s internal expert on where we can build large, attractive businesses in de-regulated domestic and international markets.

- Develop and maintain the backlog of new market opportunities for our distributed battery business, educating the team on what geographies are ‘on deck’.

- Own the business case for taking Base to a new market.
